Vicinity of hot air sources The purpose of this requirement is to eliminate known factors contributing to false detection caused by refraction. Refraction is a phenomenon taking place when a wave passes from one medium to another, resulting in a change of its direction. It also applies to ultrasonic waves traveling across a boundary created by cold and hot air areas. NOTE: General guidelines contained herein help to minimize the risk of unwanted reflections, but are not exhaustive due to the nature of the phenomenon. Additional tests on representative vehicles are recommended.
Front grille and air intakes Description Hot air pushed out of the engine compartment through the front grilles or air intakes produces hot air accumulation in the bumper vicinity. This may lead to unwanted reflections of ultrasonic waves and change their propagation path. This is particularly important if the correct system integration was achieved by use of near field filters or similar feature, which minimizes the influence of the vehicle’s own geometry on the echo received by the sensors.

Mechanical design Sensor holder Water drainage Water drainage is necessary to ensure proper operation of sensors. Residual water has a tendency to flow upward in narrow gaps due to capillary action. This may cause unwanted coupling between the sensor housing and its membrane. When water residues freeze and expand, additional pressure on the sensor housing may be generated resulting in sensor deactivation or false detections.
Mechanical design Sensor integration with holder The holder design and sensor integration shall guarantee no gap condition between the sensor housing and the DCR in the range of expected tolerances.
Mechanical design Drainage hole location The sensor holder shall comprise an aperture, which prevents water accumulation and ensures it can freely drain away from DCR area. Comment00361985 The drainage aperture shall be as close as possible to the decopling ring. This location is convenient to evacuate water that may accumulate in the DCR vicinity after situations like a pressure wash.
Mechanical design Drainage hole The geometry of the drainage hole shall create a cut perpendicular to the ground plane of the vehicle and large enough to fully fit a square with a side of: [shall] minimum 4 mm (including tolerances) [Desirable] 5 mm (including tolerances)
